target: Poiché era tardi, abbiamo deciso di prendere un taxi.
english: Since it was late, we decided to take a taxi.
tip: "Poiché" – formal connector meaning 'since/because', usually at sentence start.

target: Mi ha chiesto se per caso conoscessi un buon ristorante in zona.
english: He asked me if by any chance I knew a good restaurant in the area.
tip: In a reported question after a past verb, use the imperfect subjunctive: mi ha chiesto se conoscessi, asked if I knew.

target: Se avessi studiato, avrei superato l'esame.
english: If I had studied, I would have passed the exam.
tip: For an unreal past regret, use se plus avessi studiato (past subjunctive) then avrei superato (past conditional).

target: Quando si è stanchi, tutto sembra più difficile.
english: When one is tired, everything seems harder.
tip: "Si è" – impersonal with essere, adjective agrees in plural.

target: Pur sapendo la verità, ha deciso di non dire niente.
english: Despite knowing the truth, he decided not to say anything.
tip: "Pur" + gerund – concessive: 'despite/although doing'.

target: Le decisioni vengono prese durante le riunioni.
english: Decisions are made during meetings.
tip: Venire plus a past participle forms the passive for actions: vengono prese means are taken or made.

target: La riunione sta per cominciare; prendete posto per favore.
english: The meeting is about to start – please take your seats.
tip: Stare per plus an infinitive means to be about to do something: sta per cominciare = is about to start.

target: Pur essendo stanco, ha continuato a lavorare fino a tardi.
english: Despite being tired, he kept working until late.
tip: Pur plus a gerund means although or despite: pur essendo stanco = although being tired.

target: Non riesco a dormire quando fa troppo caldo la notte.
english: I can't sleep when it's too hot at night.
tip: Italian frames cannot as not managing to: non riesco a dormire is literally I do not succeed in sleeping, using riuscire, not potere.

target: Per quanto ne sappia, nessuno ha ancora trovato una soluzione.
english: As far as I know, nobody has found a solution yet.
tip: "Per quanto" (as far as / however much) triggers subjunctive.

target: Il progetto è da rifare.
english: The project needs redoing.
tip: Essere da plus an infinitive means still to be done: il progetto è da rifare says the project is to be redone, it still needs it.

target: Spende soldi come se fossero acqua fresca.
english: He spends money as if it were nothing.
tip: Come se takes the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive, never the present: come se fossero = as if they were.

target: Ho da fare tutto il pomeriggio; ci vediamo stasera.
english: I have things to do all afternoon – see you tonight.
tip: Avere da plus an infinitive lists what you must do; ho da fare on its own also just means I am busy.

target: Questa storia va raccontata per non dimenticare il passato.
english: This story must be told so as not to forget the past.
tip: Andare plus a past participle carries obligation: questa storia va raccontata means the story must be told.

target: A meno che non cambi idea, parto domani mattina presto.
english: Unless I change my mind, I'm leaving early tomorrow morning.
tip: That non after a meno che is a filler, not a real negative: a meno che non cambi idea just means unless I change my mind.

target: Cerco un hotel che abbia una vista panoramica sul mare.
english: I'm looking for a hotel that has a panoramic sea view.
tip: When the hotel is only hoped for, not a specific one, the relative verb goes subjunctive: cerco un hotel che abbia, not che ha.

target: Senza che nessuno se ne accorga, è uscita di nascosto ieri.
english: Without anyone noticing, she snuck out yesterday.
tip: "Senza che" (without) requires the subjunctive.

target: Anzi, penso il contrario.
english: On the contrary, I think the opposite.
tip: 'Anzi' corrects or strengthens a previous statement.

target: Gli ho detto di non preoccuparsi.
english: I told him not to worry.
tip: A command reported with dire turns into di plus an infinitive: ho detto di non preoccuparsi = I told him not to worry.

target: Continua a piovere da tre giorni senza interruzione.
english: It has been raining for three days without interruption.
tip: Continua a piovere da tre giorni uses the present with da where English switches to has been raining for three days.

target: Il treno sta per partire; dobbiamo correre al binario.
english: The train is about to leave – we have to run to the platform.
tip: "Stare per" signals something is on the verge of happening.

target: Scusa, sai dove si trova la stazione centrale qui vicino?
english: Sorry, do you know where the central station is near here?
tip: "Scusa" (tu) vs "Mi scusi" (Lei) marks the formality register shift.

target: Saranno le tre del pomeriggio; il sole è ancora alto.
english: It must be about three in the afternoon – the sun is still high.
tip: The future can express a guess about the present, not future time: saranno le tre means it must be about three now.

target: Quindi, è inutile continuare a discutere.
english: So, it's pointless to keep arguing.
tip: Each verb fixes its own preposition before an infinitive, and continuare locks in a: continuare a discutere = to keep arguing.

target: Mi sono fatto aiutare da un esperto.
english: I got help from an expert.
tip: Farsi plus an infinitive means getting something done for you: mi sono fatto aiutare da un esperto = I got an expert to help me.

target: Si è messo a ridere senza alcun motivo apparente.
english: He started laughing for no apparent reason.
tip: Mettersi a is literally to put yourself to something, marking a sudden start: si è messo a ridere = he burst out laughing.

target: Cerco di capire il tuo punto di vista sulla questione.
english: I'm trying to understand your point of view on the matter.
tip: Cercare alone means to look for, but cercare di plus an infinitive means to try to: cerco di capire = I am trying to understand.

target: Sebbene il viaggio sia stato lungo, ne è valsa la pena.
english: Although the trip was long, it was worth it.
tip: Sebbene always takes the subjunctive, even about real facts: sebbene il viaggio sia stato lungo reports a trip that truly was long.

target: Mi ha rimproverato di non averla avvisata del cambiamento di programma.
english: She reproached me for not having informed her of the schedule change.
tip: Where English says reproached me for not having done, Italian uses di plus a past infinitive: di non averla avvisata.

target: Ha detto: 'Qui si mangia bene.' Ha detto che li si mangiava bene.
english: She said: 'The food is good here.' She said the food was good there.
tip: In reported speech, here-words shift to there-words: qui becomes lì, so qui si mangia bene turns into lì si mangiava bene.
